response: The global food system faces unprecedented pressure as the world population is projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, requiring a 60% increase in food production, while climate change, water scarcity (including rapid depletion of the Ogallala Aquifer), and soil degradation (affecting 33% of arable land) are already reducing agricultural productivity. Agriculture itself contributes roughly 25% of greenhouse gas emissions, and approximately one-third of all food produced is lost or wasted. Multiple solutions are being explored, including precision agriculture, vertical farming, alternative proteins, drought-resistant crops, and regenerative farming practices, along with policy changes to subsidies, trade, and carbon pricing. The central challenge is scaling these solutions while ensuring food remains affordable and accessible to vulnerable populations.
